reason: Plugin load configuration is read before any plugin runs, so no plugin can claim it. The config loader turns this subtree into the plugin list that the server then starts.
The hub reads this subtree directly and passes it to the PPPoE subsystem at startup. Delivery does not go through the plugin config RPC, so no WantsConfigRoots entry names it.
The hub reads the SMART monitor settings directly from the config tree and builds the storage manager configuration. No plugin is involved.

System settings are applied by components inside the daemon (kernel tuning, console, update, conntrack, authorization, archive), each reading the subtree from the config tree. No plugin RPC carries them.
